text:
Dr. George Isaacson
Cardiologist
45 Inkerman Street
Caulfield 3162
19/1/2007
Dear Dr. Isaacson,
RE: Mr. Jing Zu
I am writing to refer Mr Zu, a 72-year-old retired school teacher whose features are suggestive of ischemic heart disease.
Mr. Zu has been suffering from hypertension, ischemic heart disease and congestive heart failure for many years. Accordingly, he has been commenced on Lasix, Arginine, enalapril and nifedipine.
On 3/1/20117, Mr. Zu firstly presented with angina on exertion which was neither relieved with Arginine nor resting. His examination was unremarkable apart from hypertension (blood pressure was 160/90) and bilateral basal crepitations. On 15/1/2007, his condition deteriorated. He came complaining of progressive dyspnea and orthopnea . His examination revealed lower limb edema up to the knees in addition to chest crepitations extending to the middle lung zones. Consequently, Lasix dose was increased to 80 mg.
Today, the patient presented with a history of angina episode on mild exertion which lasted for 10 minutes yesterday. However, his complaint of dyspnea decreased. ECG confirmed anterolateral myocardial ischemic changes.
In view of the above, I would appreciate if you provide an assessment of Mr Zu and advice regarding treatment and management his condition as you see suitable. Should you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely, 
Doctor
